analysis.requirement: R3 — Identified awareness effect: is the claim that awareness changes realized shelter access identified (experiment, natural experiment, or strong quasi-experiment with recorded timing of outreach/awareness/departure/arrival), or must it be narrowed to "modeled shelter use is sensitive to ASSUMED awareness"?
exists_defensible: The chapter (both forms) already executes the requirement's fallback narrowing for its A-D scenarios: universal awareness is disclosed as an assumption making every access figure an upper bound, and it is correctly noted that the limitation 'applies identically to all three scenarios, so it does not affect the comparison between them, which is what this chapter claims' (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:289; docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:937-946). The chapter's central capacity-vs-placement contrast is therefore awareness-invariant by construction.

A genuinely local, event-specific awareness measurement exists and is the sourced value of V29: Hines et al. 2021 'Stories from the Outside' (PSU HRAC), N=73 unhoused Portland-area adults surveyed June 2021 about the September 2020 event — 65% did not hear about the shelters (aware 26/73 = 0.356), 10 of 26 aware attempted access (0.385), with caveats recorded (retrospective ~9 months, non-probability sample, Wilson CI 0.25-0.47) (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:42-63; Geography/data/registry/variables.csv rows V29-V30).

A two-point model sensitivity to assumed awareness exists and is archived: omniscient arms (pAwareInit=1.0, E0null) versus measured-awareness arms (pAwareInit=0.356, ER-A/C/D x seeds 42-44) — verified in run manifests (docs/runs/phase-e/ER-A-n6842-seed42/simulation.json 'pAwareInit': 0.356; docs/runs/phase-e/E0null-A-n6842-seed42/simulation.json 'pAwareInit': 1.0). At 0.356 awareness all three arms shelter an identical 1,215 of 6,842 at seed 42 with beds empty (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:93-95), demonstrating in-model that assumed awareness, not capacity, becomes binding.

The double-counting logic for outreach is defensibly reasoned: baseline-real sets lambdaOutreachPerDay=0 because the survey's 0.356 is awareness DURING the event and already embeds whatever outreach occurred (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:43-46).

Registered-prediction discipline covers the awareness pipeline: P-E1's 0.356 x 0.385 = 13.7% attempt arithmetic was registered before the runs and scored a MISS (realized attempt share among the aware 0.502), with the alphaHazard arithmetic error documented as a correction rather than edited away (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:20-41).

The direction of the one external calibration discrepancy is consistent with the awareness evidence and is used with restraint in the results docs: 'Everyone is assumed to know the shelters exist... a Portland State survey found 65%... had never heard of the shelters. So arm A's 30.1% is an optimistic upper bound' (docs/final/README_RESULTS.md:217-219).
missing: Any identification design linking awareness to realized access is ABSENT: no randomized or phased outreach intervention, no randomized-encouragement design, no natural experiment from staggered communications, and no quasi-experiment on outreach timing or geographic boundaries exists anywhere in the repo (no such data, runs, or analysis found; the registry itself states 'a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record' — Geography/data/registry/variables.csv row V41).

Real-world timing records are ABSENT on all four required events: no outreach-contact timestamps (V41/A-31), no awareness-onset timing (the Hines survey is retrospective by ~9 months and cross-sectional — docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:61-63), no real departure times, and no real arrival times. The only temporal observations for the event are shelter opening dates (Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2020-09.csv rows 2-3), a one-night occupancy snapshot (~90 + ~40 on Sept 16), and a single 211 datum (waits >1h; 21 clean-air calls on Sept 15) (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:69-71). All departure/arrival times in docs/runs are model outputs.

The registered awareness sensitivity SWEEP was never run: variables.csv row V29 records sweep range '0.25-0.47 (Wilson 95% CI on 26/73); swept', but every archived manifest carries pAwareInit of exactly 0.356 or 1.0 (grep over docs/runs: only these two values appear). No interval over the survey's CI exists in any archive.

The registered outreach-rate sweep was never run: variables.csv row V41 records 'swept 0-0.2 per day including 0', but all 62 archived manifests carry lambdaOutreachPerDay = 0.0 (grep over docs/runs). The only awareness-conversion channel in the model has never been exercised at a nonzero rate.

The chapter contains no awareness-effect result at all: the Phase-E measured-awareness runs are absent from both manuscript forms, and the tex still frames per-resident awareness probability as a future extension — 'Giving each resident a probability of knowing, swept across a range, would turn each figure from a single upper bound into an interval' (Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:1069-1074) — although exactly that mechanism is implemented (V29/ELayerSampler) and archived (docs/runs/phase-e/).

Individual-level microdata linking awareness status to attempt and arrival is ABSENT: the repo holds only transcribed aggregates of the Hines survey (26/73, 10/26), not respondent-level records, channels, or timing (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:50-58).

The E9 occupancy calibration that would fit the awareness-to-arrival pipeline to the one observed record is deferred on record and no E9 run archive exists (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:25-26, 84; no E9 family in docs/runs/).
implementable_with_existing_data: Run the already-registered pAwareInit sweep over the Wilson CI 0.25-0.47 (plus a 0-1 grid) using the existing batch generator scripts/make_batch_params_E.py (which already parameterizes pAwareInit at lines 57/84) and the existing gate scripts/verify_E_runs.py; report every absolute access figure as an interval rather than a point. This directly delivers the requirement's fallback: 'modeled shelter use is sensitive to ASSUMED awareness', quantified.

Run the registered lambdaOutreachPerDay sweep 0-0.2/day (A-31 range, code path already in GisAgent hourly conversion per variables.csv V41) as an in-model phased-outreach analog — explicitly labeled an assumption sweep, since the rate is unsourced.

Execute the deferred E9 calibration with data already in the repo: fit (alphaHazard, optionally pAwareInit within its CI) so the historical-reference configuration (Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2020-09.csv, n=2037 2020-vintage population, docs/runs/historical-reference/histref-n2037-seed42) reproduces the censored occupancy record (~90 right-censored at 99 + 40 of 99; docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:70) — reported as calibration/partial identification, never as an identified causal effect.

A variance-attribution / tornado analysis across already-archived arms (E0null pAwareInit=1.0 vs ER pAwareInit=0.356 vs closure/smoke variants in docs/runs/phase-e, scenario-e, scenario-e-v2) quantifying how much of the omniscient-to-realistic access drop is attributable to the awareness parameter versus the hazard-departure and barrier parameters.

Text reconciliation implementable today: import the Phase-E awareness sensitivity into the chapter (or explicitly cite it), cite Hines et al. 2021 and the 65% figure in the manuscript (currently only in docs/final/README_RESULTS.md:217-219 and docs/chapter/SUBMIT.md:298, never in the chapter), fix the stale future-work paragraph (tex:1069-1074), and recondition the present-tense headline sentences (md:27, md:315).
needs_new_empirical_data: Cluster-randomized encouragement design: randomize timing/intensity of outreach information contacts across encampment clusters during a preparedness exercise or the next smoke event, recording contact timestamp, a short verbal awareness check, stated intent, and timestamped shelter arrivals (door tally); requires IRB protections for a vulnerable population and partner outreach organizations.

Stepped-wedge (phased) outreach rollout with shelter door-count time series: outreach waves staggered by area on a schedule, with nightly per-facility sign-in counts, enabling difference-in-differences on arrivals.

Prospective intercept/panel survey during an actual event recording WHEN each respondent first heard of shelters, through which channel, and whether/when they departed and arrived — replacing the current retrospective 9-month recall instrument (Hines N=73).

Timestamped arrival logging at shelters (even a paper log with hour of arrival and a mobility/awareness intake question) during any future activation — the minimum record the requirement names, which no agency kept in 2020 per the repo's audits.
needs_external_acquisition: 211info call logs for September 2020 (timestamped clean-air-shelter calls, wait times) — candidate source: 211info (Oregon/SW Washington nonprofit); the repo holds only one newspaper sentence about them (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:71). If obtainable, call timing could serve as a communications-timing quasi-experiment instrument.

Multnomah County JOHS after-action report, shelter sign-in sheets, or nightly occupancy logs for the Sept 2020 activation — candidate source: Joint Office of Homeless Services via Oregon public records request; the repo's own audit records these were never obtained (docs/final/SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md per validation inventory; A-04 blocking).

Respondent-level microdata from Hines et al. 2021 (N=73), including any channel/timing items not in the published summary — candidate source: PSU Homelessness Research & Action Collaborative (survey verified by the author at pdx.edu per docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:47-48).

Outreach-contact logs from the 27 outreach/mutual-aid partners named in JOHS press releases (docs/science/DATA_SOURCES.md:62-64 per data inventory) — candidate source: JOHS and partner organizations; would ground lambdaOutreachPerDay, currently unsourced (A-31).

Public-alerting records (timestamps and geographic scope of any emergency notifications during Sept 10-19, 2020) — candidate source: Portland Bureau of Emergency Management / Multnomah County Emergency Management; could establish whether staggered communications existed at all (prerequisite for any natural experiment).

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "the model over-predicts the one observed occupancy record by 1.5-15.6x... The over-prediction is attributed to assuming universal shelter awareness against local evidence that 65% had never heard of the shelters" — presented as 'already in the chapter'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Doubly overreaching. First, the chapter's Calibration subsection contains neither the bracket nor the awareness attribution — it states no suitable record exists (Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:929-935, verified). Second, the attribution itself is a residual attribution from a single censored one-night observation: with the 99-bed capacity unit unconfirmed (A-04 blocking), the 2019-PIT population vintage, and every hazard coefficient assumed, the discrepancy cannot be attributed to awareness versus these competing explanations. Direction-consistency with the survey is a plausibility argument, not identification.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: V29 pAwareInit sweep range "0.25-0.47 (Wilson 95% CI on 26/73); swept" (sweep flag: yes)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: No archived run uses any pAwareInit value other than 0.356 or 1.0 (verified by grep across all docs/runs manifests). The registered CI sweep was never executed; 'swept' overstates the evidence base for any awareness-sensitivity interval.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: V41 lambdaOutreachPerDay "swept 0-0.2 per day including 0 (no outreach)"
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: All 62 archived manifests carrying the parameter record lambdaOutreachPerDay = 0.0 (verified by grep). Only the zero point has ever run; the model's sole awareness-conversion channel is untested at any nonzero rate.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents" / "The present system shelters 30.1% of residents" (present-tense, unconditioned)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Reads as a claim about the real system while awareness is modeled as universal. The repo's own record contradicts the realized-access reading twice over: the local survey found 65% never heard of the shelters (docs/final/README_RESULTS.md:217-219), and the project's own measured-awareness arms shelter ~17.8% (1,215/6,842) not 30.1% (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:93-95). The upper-bound hedge exists (md:289) but not in these sentences.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "the binding constraint moves from doors/geography to awareness and willingness, which no placement can fix" (and the '35.6% awareness ceiling' framing throughout Phase-E/Scenario-E scoring)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Within its prediction-document context this is candidly framed, but as a claim about awareness it rests on one retrospective non-probability survey point (N=73) fed through an assumed logistic hazard whose intercept derivation was itself scored a MISS (realized attempt share 0.502 vs targeted 0.385, 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:28-41). If this sentence migrates into a deliverable as a finding about the real system rather than a model consequence of assumed awareness, it exceeds identification. The safe wording the requirement demands — modeled use is sensitive to assumed awareness — is available and should travel with it.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "A model of awareness is the most valuable single addition... Giving each resident a probability of knowing, swept across a range, would turn each figure from a single upper bound into an interval" (stated as not yet done)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Not overreach but a staleness defect that undermines the R3 defense: the mechanism is implemented (V29, ELayerSampler) and run (docs/runs/phase-e ER arms at 0.356). The chapter simultaneously omits its own awareness-sensitivity evidence and understates the project's actual state; a reviewer discovering the archives would question which claims correspond to which model.

proposed_methods: Partial-identification / bounds analysis: with one interval-censored occupancy observation (OCC >=90 censored at 99; CJ = 40) and the survey CI on awareness (0.25-0.47), report the identified SET of (awareness, attempt-hazard) pairs consistent with the record — Manski-style bounds on the awareness effect — instead of any point attribution.

Approximate Bayesian Computation (or interval-censored likelihood) calibration of (pAwareInit, alphaHazard) against the historical-reference run configuration, propagating the joint posterior through all headline access figures so every absolute number carries an awareness-uncertainty band; this is the deferred E9 made rigorous.

Global sensitivity analysis (Latin hypercube or Sobol indices) over the assumed behavioral block (pAwareInit, lambdaOutreach, alphaHazard, bRisk, wOfficial, barrier costs), reporting the awareness parameter's share of output variance — replaces the current one-factor-at-a-time posture, which for awareness has not even been run.

In-model encouragement analog, honestly labeled: sweep lambdaOutreachPerDay over its registered 0-0.2/day range and report the marginal arrival gain per unit outreach as a model-derived policy elasticity under assumptions, not an estimate.

For future identification: cluster-randomized encouragement (outreach contact randomized by encampment cluster with recorded contact/awareness/departure/arrival timestamps) or a stepped-wedge phased rollout during a preparedness exercise; analysis by intention-to-treat difference-in-differences on timestamped door counts, with discrete-time survival models of departure using time-varying awareness — this is the only route to an identified awareness->access effect.

Immediate text remedy (zero new runs required): adopt the requirement's narrowed claim verbatim wherever awareness touches an absolute number — 'modeled shelter use is sensitive to assumed awareness' — recondition md:27/md:315, correct SUBMIT.md:298 to match what the chapter actually says, cite Hines et al. 2021 in the chapter, and present the calibration discrepancy's awareness attribution as one candidate explanation among the enumerated alternatives (capacity unit, population vintage, hazard coefficients).
analysis.priority_rationale: For the chapter as currently scoped, R3 is a moderate-severity requirement handled by the fallback: the A-D comparison is awareness-invariant by design and the universal-awareness upper-bound hedge is present and well-worded (md:289; tex:937-946), so the title's core claim — capacity is not access — rests on geography and admission mechanics identified within-model, not on awareness. But R3 becomes load-bearing at three places the project cannot avoid. First, every ABSOLUTE figure a policymaker would quote (30.1% sheltered today, 550 refused, the 1.5-15.6x calibration bracket) is conditional on an awareness assumption the repo's own evidence contradicts (65% never heard; the measured-awareness arms shelter 17.8% not 30.1%), and two headline sentences state those figures in unconditioned present tense. Second, the calibration discrepancy's attribution to universal awareness (SUBMIT.md:298, README_RESULTS, TECHNICAL_REFERENCE) is the project's bridge between model and reality, and it is a residual attribution from one censored observation with unidentified competing explanations — a top-journal reviewer will press exactly here. Third, the entire Phase-E/Scenario-E program's headline ('awareness, not doors, becomes the binding constraint') is an awareness-effect claim built on one N=73 retrospective survey point pushed through assumed hazard coefficients whose registered intercept derivation already missed. The cheapest high-value fixes are fully in-repo: run the registered-but-never-executed pAwareInit CI sweep and lambdaOutreach sweep (all archived manifests show only 0.356/1.0 and 0.0 — the registry's 'swept' flags currently overstate), execute the deferred E9 calibration as explicit partial identification, and align the chapter's stale future-work paragraph and SUBMIT.md with the project's actual state. True identification of awareness->realized access requires new field data (randomized or phased outreach with timestamped arrivals) that no archive or acquirable 2020 record can substitute for; until then, every deliverable should carry the narrowed claim.
